# DeckPal MCP tools

**29 tools: 18 read, 11 write**, in the order `tools/list` returns them, plus 3 capability-gated read tools shown only to a token holding the Deck-E improvement capability. A read-only connection is shown the 18 read tools and none of the writes.

Every write previews by default (`dry_run` defaults to true) except `deck_strategy`, whose description says it writes at once. "destructive" is MCP's meaning: the tool may change or remove existing data, not only add to it. What can be undone, and how, is in `decisions/2026/2026-10-12-mcp-tool-surface-and-write-safety.md`.

| tool | title | kind | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`health`](#health) | DeckPal health & data freshness | read | Check that deckpal-mcp can reach Postgres and deckpal-api, how fast those hops are, and how fresh the data is: catalog counts (cards/variants/sets), owned totals, the last sync run per job with its status, and price freshness per source. |
| [`collection_summary`](#collection_summary) | Collection summary | read | The default entry point for collection questions: distinct cards owned, total copies, sets with ownership, estimated USD value (with the unpriced-variant count), the top-N owned cards by value, and the 5 nearest-complete sets for your default goal. |
| [`collection_log`](#collection_log) | Collection change log | read | The audit trail of collection changes (collection_event), newest first: when, which card/variant, the quantity delta and resulting quantity, who wrote it (source: web UI, deckpal-mcp, imports) and any note. |
| [`collection_value`](#collection_value) | Collection value & movers | read | Estimated collection value right now (per currency, best market price × quantity), how it changed over a window (from the daily value snapshots), and the biggest owned price movers vs their 30-day average. |

### `health` — DeckPal health & data freshness

read · annotations `{"title":"DeckPal health & data freshness","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

<a id="search_cards"></a>

### `search_cards` — Search the card catalog

read · annotations `{"title":"Search the card catalog","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Search cards by NAME or by their PRINTED RULES TEXT. `query` matches CARD names only — never a set name, a series name or an artist. To narrow to a set, put the set in `set_id` — it takes the set NAME as readily as the id. Searching for a set name in `query` always returns nothing, however many ways you spell it. Accent-insensitive substring, with `text` searches attack names/effects and Ability names/effects. This — not web research — is how to answer "which cards do X"; combine it with `damage` for attack damage modifiers. Optional filters: set, category, rarity, Standard legality, owned-only, not-owned (exclude_owned), and minimum USD market value. Each row shows owned quantity and best USD market price. Rows sharing a name sort cheapest first. PREFER THE CHEAPEST PRINTING OF THE SAME CARD — a regular and a Special Illustration Rare play identically and can differ by hundreds of dollars — but SAME NAME IS NOT SAME CARD: this game reuses names across sets for cards with different HP and different text, and 218 Standard-legal names here are more than one card. When a page contains several cards under one name this tool says so, and groups the ids that really are interchangeable; swap only within one of those groups. Use this to find cards or list slices of the collection; for full detail on ONE card (variants, tiers, per-source prices) use get_card instead, and for set completion use set_progress.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string |  |  | One card's printed name, or part of it — 'charizard', 'iono'. A plain substring match, accent- and case-insensitive. NOT a search engine: OR, AND, quotes and wildcards are matched literally and will find nothing. This field only sees the NAME — use `text` for printed attacks and Abilities. It does not see artwork, rarity, popularity, or whether a card is good or admired or a bargain. For any of those, research it. |
| `text` | string[] |  |  | Up to 6 literal substrings from printed rules text (attack/Ability name or effect). Every term must match. Use this, not web research, for "which cards do X" questions. `%` and `_` are literal characters. |
| `text_same_attack` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default) requires all text terms — and damage, when present — on one matching attack or Ability. false allows terms to occur on different attacks/Abilities of the same card. |
| `damage` | "x" \| "+" \| "-" |  |  | Attack damage suffix: x matches either × or literal x; + and - match those literal suffixes. |
| `set_id` | string |  |  | One set, by id ('me05') or by NAME ('Pitch Black'). A name that matches several sets comes back as a choice. |
| `category` | "Pokemon" \| "Trainer" \| "Energy" |  |  | Limit to one card category. |
| `rarity` | string |  |  | Exact rarity name, case-insensitive, e.g. 'Double Rare'. |
| `owned_only` | boolean |  | `false` | true → only cards you own at least one copy of (any variant). |
| `exclude_owned` | boolean |  | `false` | true → only cards you do NOT own (owned quantity 0 or no row) — the filter for "cards I do not own" / buy-recommendation asks. Mirrors owned_only the other way; do not pass both. |
| `standard_legal` | boolean |  |  | Filter on Standard-format legality (card.legal_standard). |
| `tag` | "Tera" \| "Ancient" \| "Future" |  |  | Only printings with this tag. Rows show tags too. |
| `min_value_usd` | number |  |  | Only cards worth at least this many USD. 0 means no minimum and is ignored. Any value ABOVE 0 also drops cards with no price at all, so use 0.01 for "only cards that have a price". |
| `page` | integer |  | `1` | Page number, 1-based. |
| `page_size` | integer |  | `50` | Rows per page (default 50, hard cap 200). |

### `get_card` — Card detail (variants, tiers, prices)

read · annotations `{"title":"Card detail (variants, tiers, prices)","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Full detail for ONE card: identity, rarity, HP, regulation mark, legality, set and collector number, and FULL RULES TEXT — Abilities (name, type, effect), attacks (cost, name, damage, effect), the Trainer/Tool/Energy effect line, and weakness/resistance plus retreat — so the card can be advised on by what it DOES, not from memory. Then every printing variant with its kind, completion tier, owned quantity, per-source market prices, and TCGplayer link. Identify the card by TCGdex card_id (e.g. 'me05-084') or by name plus optional set_id/number — an ambiguous name returns the candidate list rather than guessing. For browsing many cards use search_cards instead.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `card_id` | string |  |  | TCGdex card id, e.g. 'me05-084'. Wins over name if both given. |
| `name` | string |  |  | Card name (exact or substring, accent-insensitive). |
| `set_id` | string |  |  | Narrow a name lookup to one set, by id ('me05') or by NAME ('Pitch Black'). |
| `number` | string |  |  | Narrow a name lookup to a collector number, e.g. '084'. |

<a id="set_progress"></a>

### `set_progress` — Check set completion

read · annotations `{"title":"Check set completion","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Completion progress toward the three goals (complete = one of any variant per card, master = every standard-tier variant, grandmaster = every variant), plus goal 'numbered' = the regular numbered set only: one of any variant of each card numbered 1 up to the printed set total (the 165 in "006/165"), leaving out secret rares numbered above it and unnumbered subset cards (TG01, GG01). Numbered is computed live and reported as not available for a set with no printed total. Without set_id: every set YOU ALREADY OWN SOMETHING FROM, sorted by completion of the requested goal (a set you own nothing from does not appear — pass its name as set_id to reach it, or pass all_sets: true to list EVERY set in the catalog newest-first with its card count and how many you own, even zero). With set_id: that set's three goal lines plus the paged list of missing cards/variants for the requested goal with the cheapest USD price each, and the total cost to finish (unpriced items counted separately, never $0). Goal defaults to your default goal setting. Not for whole-collection stats — use collection_summary.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `set_id` | string |  |  | One set, by id ('me05') or by NAME ('Pitch Black'). Omit it for the overview of sets you have progress in. |
| `all_sets` | boolean |  | `false` | Without set_id: list EVERY set in the catalog (id, name, series, release date, card count, and your owned count — 0 is fine) ordered by release date descending, instead of only the sets you already own something from. Use this for release-order or "what sets exist" questions. |
| `goal` | "complete" \| "master" \| "grandmaster" \| "numbered" |  |  | Which goal to rank by / list missing cards for. Defaults to user_settings.default_goal. 'numbered' answers questions about the regular, main or numbered set without secret rares (cards 1 to the printed total, one of any variant each); it is never the default. |
| `rarity` | string[] |  |  | With set_id: list ONLY these rarities, e.g. ['Illustration rare']. Exact names, case-insensitive; the rarity of every missing row is shown in the output so you can see the vocabulary. |
| `rarity_exclude` | string[] |  |  | With set_id: leave these rarities OUT, e.g. ['Special illustration rare']. Rarity is NOT variant tier — an Illustration Rare and a Special Illustration Rare are both tier 'standard', so a tier filter cannot express this. To leave out the secret rares above the printed total, use goal 'numbered' instead. |
| `page` | integer |  | `1` | Page number, 1-based. |
| `page_size` | integer |  | `50` | Rows per page (default 50, hard cap 200). |

<a id="card_price_history"></a>

### `card_price_history` — Historical prices for one card (OHLC)

read · annotations `{"title":"Historical prices for one card (OHLC)","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Historical OHLC price series for one card by TCGdex id (e.g. sv03.5-151 or base1-1). Returns bounded pages of complete price points across every printing variant. Start with offset=0, then continue with the next_offset shown in the result TEXT, keeping the same card_id, range and currency, until next_offset=none. Offsets count points in API order, with one record for each empty variant. For CURRENT prices use get_card instead. range: 30d|3m|6m|1y|18m|2y (default 3m). currency: USD|EUR|JPY (default USD). An empty series means there are no recorded observations for that card/range/currency — not that the price is zero, not a fabricated trend, not current price.

Grounded on `grain`, an agent:

  MAY assert — open/close/high/low/mean/median of a bucket; the exact dates
  and values of the period's high and low (`highOn`/`lowOn` are TRUE DAILY
  FACTS that survive the rollup); trend across buckets; and volatility
  DERIVED from OHLC (Parkinson or Garman-Klass), never a stored variance.

  MAY NOT assert — any specific day's price inside a week or month bucket
  other than the two extremes; the path between them; durations ("stayed
  under $5 for eleven days"); or a second/third dip or spike within one
  bucket. Those are the things the rollup genuinely destroys.

"It dipped to $4.00 on the 12th" is licensed if and only if `lowOn` says the
12th and `low` says $4.00.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `card_id` | string | yes |  | TCGdex canonical card id, e.g. 'sv03.5-151' or 'base1-1'. Required, non-blank. |
| `range` | "30d" \| "3m" \| "6m" \| "1y" \| "18m" \| "2y" |  | `"3m"` | History window: 30d \| 3m \| 6m \| 1y \| 18m \| 2y. Default 3m. |
| `currency` | "USD" \| "EUR" \| "JPY" |  | `"USD"` | Currency: USD \| EUR \| JPY. Default USD. Values are in major units (dollars/euros/yen) — never cents. |
| `offset` | integer |  | `0` | Start at 0. Continue with next_offset from the result text, using the same card_id, range and currency. Counts complete points, plus one record per empty variant. |

<a id="decks"></a>

### `decks` — Browse decks

read · annotations `{"title":"Browse decks","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Read decks. Without deck_id: the deck index (id, name, format, version, card count, legality, value, battle record). With deck_id: full deck detail — version, win/loss record, strategy-guide presence, battle-log count — plus any requested includes: cards (the deck list with owned counts), validate (format-legality violations), pricing (the buy-the-missing-cards gap analysis: owned vs needed per card, cost to close, TCGplayer mass-entry lines + cart deep link(s) the user can open to pre-fill a TCGplayer cart), testhand (a sample opening hand), strategy (the FULL strategy-guide markdown — the header line only ever reports its heading and length, so ask for this include to actually read it). Read-only. To create or edit a deck use save_deck; to delete use delete_deck. Deck intelligence has its own tools: deck_strategy (reads the same guide, and is the only way to WRITE one), battle_logs (game results per version), deck_history (version timeline, snapshots, revert).

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string |  |  | One deck, by UUID or by NAME. Omit to list all decks with their ids. |
| `deleted` | boolean |  | `false` | true → show DELETED decks (the recycle bin) instead of live ones. Restore one with delete_deck(restore:true). |
| `include` | "cards" \| "validate" \| "pricing" \| "testhand" \| "strategy"[] |  |  | Extra sections to fetch for one deck: 'cards', 'validate', 'pricing', 'testhand', 'strategy' (the whole guide text). Ignored without deck_id. |
| `page` | integer |  | `1` | Without deck_id: page of the index, 100 decks a page. |

<a id="save_deck"></a>

### `save_deck` — Create or edit a deck

write, destructive, idempotent · annotations `{"title":"Create or edit a deck","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Create a deck (omit deck_id) or edit one (pass deck_id): rename, change format, and reconcile its card list to the given cards array in one all-or-nothing write. To create from a PTCG Live decklist pass ptcgl_text instead of cards (creation only). Card ids are TCGdex ids (e.g. sv01-25). When choosing a card_id, use the cheapest printing OF THE SAME CARD unless the user asked for a specific rarity or art: printings of one card are gameplay-identical and can differ by hundreds of dollars (a Special Illustration Rare vs the regular version). SAME NAME IS NOT SAME CARD, and this is the trap — the game reuses names across sets for cards with different HP and different text, so the cheapest row under a name can be a different card that happens to share it. Shaymin sv08.5-087 (70 HP, $0.20) and sv10-010 (80 HP, $0.83) are not the same card. Picking wrong is SILENT: the deck still has 60 cards and is still legal, it just does not do what the list said. search_cards flags a name that is several cards and groups the ids that really are interchangeable — swap only within one of those groups, and when in doubt keep the printing the decklist named. Defaults to a dry run that prints the exact operations without executing — re-run with dry_run: false to apply. Versioning is automatic: card and format changes to a deck version that already has battle logs create a NEW version (its snapshot is kept forever — see deck_history); changes to a logless version just amend the current snapshot, so a burst of edits stays one version. Pass version_note to record WHY the list changed (e.g. 'cut Switch for Jet Energy after v2 losses to Dragapult') — future agents read it in deck_history. Strategy guides are edited with deck_strategy, not here. Not for reading (use decks) or deleting (use delete_deck).

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | "create" \| "edit" |  |  | 'create' makes a NEW deck and never touches an existing one, even if a deck of the same name exists. 'edit' changes the deck named by deck_id and never creates. Say which — leaving it out infers from deck_id, and an inference is how someone’s existing decklist gets rewritten by accident. |
| `deck_id` | string |  |  | The deck to EDIT, by UUID or by its exact name. Leave it out to create a new one. Ignored entirely when mode is 'create'. |
| `name` | string |  |  | Deck name — required when creating without ptcgl_text; renames when editing. |
| `format` | "standard" \| "expanded" \| "glc" \| "unlimited" |  |  | Deck format (default 'standard' on create; changes the format when editing). |
| `cards` | object[] |  |  | The COMPLETE target card list. The deck is reconciled to exactly this (cards not listed are removed). Omit to leave cards untouched; [] empties the deck. For each card, use the TCGdex id of the cheapest printing unless the user specified a particular rarity or art — search_cards shows prices per printing. |
| `ptcgl_text` | string |  |  | A PTCG Live decklist to import as a NEW deck (creation only, mutually exclusive with cards). Unresolvable lines are reported, not silently dropped. When generating a decklist, use the cheapest printing of each card (set + number) unless the user requested a specific one — use search_cards to verify which printing is cheapest. |
| `version_note` | string |  |  | Why the card list is changing (max 500 chars) — recorded on the deck_version snapshot and shown in deck_history. Ignored when nothing version-relevant changes. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): only print what would happen. false: execute. |

<a id="delete_deck"></a>

### `delete_deck` — Delete a deck

write, destructive, idempotent · annotations `{"title":"Delete a deck","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Delete a deck and its card list (the collection is NOT touched — decks only reference cards). By default this is REVERSIBLE: the deck disappears from every view but keeps its version history and battle logs, and can be restored with restore:true or found again with decks(deleted:true). Defaults to a dry run that shows what would be deleted; re-run with dry_run:false to delete. purge:true is the exception — it destroys the deck, its entire version history and every battle log for good, with NO undo, and should only be used when the user has said they want it gone permanently. To remove individual cards use save_deck; to roll back to an older list use deck_history revert_to.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string | yes |  | The deck to delete, by UUID or by its exact name. |
| `purge` | boolean |  | `false` | true → destroy it permanently, taking version history and battle logs with it. NO UNDO. |
| `restore` | boolean |  | `false` | true → restore a deleted deck instead of deleting one. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): only report what would be deleted. false: delete. |

<a id="check_deck"></a>

### `check_deck` — Check a deck list

read · annotations `{"title":"Check a deck list","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Run this on every complete deck list before showing or saving it. It accepts card names or catalog ids, checks legality, evolution gaps, ownership and missing cost. Fix everything it flags, then run it again before you show or save the final list. Read-only: it saves nothing (save_deck does), and a saved deck is read with decks. For draw odds use deck_odds; for matchups, simulate_battles.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | string |  | `"standard"` | Format to check against: 'standard' (default), 'expanded', 'glc' or 'unlimited'. |
| `cards` | object[] |  |  | The list, one entry per line: exactly one of name or card_id, plus quantity. Give exactly one of cards or ptcgl_text. |
| `ptcgl_text` | string |  |  | The list as PTCG Live export text, instead of cards. |

<a id="deck_odds"></a>

### `deck_odds` — Deck odds

read · annotations `{"title":"Deck odds","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Opening-hand, Prize and draw odds for a deck, from tens of thousands of seeded shuffles (a repeat call gives the same numbers). Use it whenever someone asks how likely, how often, or what the odds are of opening, drawing or prizing something, or whether a change makes a list more consistent; never estimate odds yourself. Give a saved deck (deck_id, UUID or name) or any unsaved list (cards or ptcgl_text, as check_deck takes them), so a hypothetical change can be tested before it is saved. Without queries it reports every card; with queries it answers each one: the chance that ALL its groups are met in the opening hand, by turn N, or in the Prizes, with a 95% margin. Models a real setup (mulligan until a Basic, 6 Prizes, one draw a turn) but plays no cards: put search cards like Ultra Ball in a group to count them as outs. Read-only.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string |  |  | A saved deck, by UUID or by NAME. Give exactly one of deck_id, cards or ptcgl_text. |
| `cards` | object[] |  |  | An unsaved list, the same lines check_deck takes ({name \| card_id, quantity}). Use it to test a hypothetical change without saving it. |
| `ptcgl_text` | string |  |  | An unsaved list as PTCG Live export text. |
| `format` | string |  |  | Only with cards or ptcgl_text: the format whose printings a bare card name resolves to, as check_deck does it (default standard). It does not change the odds. |
| `queries` | object[] |  |  | Questions to answer. Omit for the default report: every card's chance to be in the opening hand, seen by turn 2, and prized. |
| `trials` | integer |  | `50000` | Shuffled games to simulate. Default 50,000 (±0.4 points at 95%); more only narrows the margin. |
| `seed` | integer |  |  | RNG seed. Omit for the fixed default, so asking twice gives the same numbers. |

<a id="simulate_battles"></a>

### `simulate_battles` — Simulate battles

read · annotations `{"title":"Simulate battles","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Play simulated games between one of the user's decks (or an unsaved list) and other decks in DeckPal's rules engine, with a heuristic CPU playing both sides, and get the numbers back. Use it to test a list against a field of opponents, to find a deck's weak matchups, or to check a change: pass the new version as compare_with (or compare_cards / compare_ptcgl_text) and both versions play the same opponents on the same seeds, and the result leads with the paired difference and a verdict. Returns, per opponent: wins, losses, draws and time-outs; win rate with its 95% interval and sample size; going-first and going-second splits; game length and how games were won or lost; how fast each side starts attacking; which Pokémon took and gave up the most Prizes; and patterns in the losses. Also: which cards played early go with winning (an association, not a cause), and which cards the engine only approximates or cannot play, which skews any matchup they are in. These are simulations by a bot, not real games. When you report them, say so, give the n and the interval with every rate, treat differences whose intervals overlap as noise, and never present them as real-world or ladder win rates. Opponents can be the user's saved decks or the built-in Standard meta pool ('meta', or 'meta:<archetype>'): one representative list per current archetype, refreshed by hand from online tournament results (the report shows each list's source, date and record, and the pool's as-of date) — so a user with one deck still has opponents. A run takes up to about 25 seconds and plays only a few dozen games, so a single result is a small sample: to tighten the intervals or settle a 'no clear difference', call again with the same inputs and the continue_token the result ends with — the games add up across calls (cumulative n, same seeds a longer run would use). Do that when the user wants more certainty or the verdict is still open, a few times at most, and stop when the verdict is clear or the intervals are narrow enough; the result says how many calls are used. Editing a deck between calls starts a fresh run.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string |  |  | The deck to test: one of the user's saved decks, by id or name. Omit it to test an unsaved list given as cards or ptcgl_text. |
| `cards` | object[] |  |  | An unsaved list to test instead of deck_id, in the same shape check_deck takes. Run check_deck on it first. |
| `ptcgl_text` | string |  |  | An unsaved list as PTCG Live export text, instead of deck_id or cards. |
| `name` | string |  |  | A label for an unsaved list in the report (for example "v4 with 2 Gwynn"). |
| `format` | string |  |  | Format used to resolve card names in an unsaved list; default standard. |
| `opponents` | string[] |  |  | Opponent decks. A saved deck by id or name (scouting lists of real opponents count) — a saved deck always wins a name clash. Or the built-in Standard META POOL: 'meta' is the top 6 archetypes by tournament share, 'meta:<archetype>' one of them (for example 'meta:Dragapult'; a name that matches none of the user's decks also finds a pool archetype). The pool is one representative list per archetype from recent online Limitless events (its as-of date, source and each list's event and record are in the report's opponent names and notes), refreshed by hand, so it is a snapshot and not today's ladder. Use it when the user has no rivals saved or asks 'how does it do into the meta'. Default: up to 6 of the user's other decks, and when they have none, the top 6 meta decks. |
| `games` | integer |  |  | Games per opponent, default 24, at most 200; rounded up to an even number. More games means narrower intervals but a longer run. The whole call stops at about 25 seconds and reports how many games it actually played. With continue_token it is the games to add on this call. |
| `speed` | "strong" \| "fast" |  |  | 'strong' (default): a CPU that searches its whole turn — better play, about 1 second a game, so a run plays roughly 25–30 games in total. 'fast': a one-step CPU — weaker play but about 20× more games, for narrower intervals. Both are bots; say which one ran. |
| `seed` | integer |  |  | Random seed, default 1. The same seed, deck and opponents replay the same games. Keep it the same when comparing two versions of a deck. |
| `compare_with` | string |  |  | PAIRED COMPARISON — use this to check whether a change makes the deck better. A second version of the deck, one of the user's saved decks by id or name (or give it unsaved as compare_cards / compare_ptcgl_text). The deck from deck_id/cards/ptcgl_text is A (before), this is B (after). Both versions play every opponent on the SAME seeds and seats, so luck mostly cancels and the result leads with the paired difference B − A, its 95% interval and a verdict that names a winner only when the interval excludes 0 — otherwise "no clear difference at this n", which is the usual honest answer for a one- or two-card change. Prefer this over two separate runs. The time budget is shared by both versions, so name 1–3 opponents and consider speed 'fast' to get enough games for a verdict. |
| `compare_cards` | object[] |  |  | Version B as an unsaved list in the same shape check_deck takes, instead of compare_with — e.g. the current deck with 2 Gwynn instead of 3. Give the WHOLE list, not just the changed lines. |
| `compare_ptcgl_text` | string |  |  | Version B as PTCG Live export text, instead of compare_with or compare_cards. |
| `compare_name` | string |  |  | A label for an unsaved version B (for example "v4 with 2 Gwynn"). |
| `continue_token` | string |  |  | CONTINUE a run for a bigger sample. Every result ends with a continue_token line. To add games, call again with the SAME inputs (the same deck_id / cards, opponents, compare_* , speed, seed) plus that token: the new games are on new seeds, exactly the games one longer run would have played, and the result is CUMULATIVE ("Cumulative over 3 calls: 92 games…") with the interval at the cumulative n. games then means games to ADD on this call. Pass the token back exactly as given and use the newest one each time. The token is signed and tied to the user and to the exact card lists: a deck edited since is refused (start a fresh run without it), as is a token older than 2 hours or after a deploy; a run allows at most 12 calls. Cumulative results leave out the per-call detail (card impact, Prize rows) that the first call shows. Continue only when the user asks for more certainty or the answer is not yet decided; stop once the verdict is clear or the intervals are narrow enough to act on — two or three continuations is usually plenty. |

<a id="deck_strategy"></a>

### `deck_strategy` — Read or write a deck strategy guide

write, destructive, idempotent · annotations `{"title":"Read or write a deck strategy guide","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Read or replace a deck's strategy guide (markdown). Omit markdown to READ the current guide in full. Pass markdown to REPLACE the whole guide (empty string clears it). There is NO dry run: a call with markdown writes at once, so show the user the new guide and get their yes first. The response reports the previous guide's first heading and length, and revert (entity_type deck_strategy) can put it back. Strategy edits NEVER bump the deck version; the guide is snapshotted with the current version, so after a version bump the new version starts from the same guide. Typical loop: read battle_logs for the current version, then update the guide here (and the card list via save_deck with a version_note). For version history use deck_history.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string | yes |  | The deck, by UUID or by its exact name. |
| `markdown` | string |  |  | The COMPLETE new guide in markdown (max 40000 chars) — replaces the whole guide, so include everything you want kept. Empty string clears the guide. Omit to read instead. |

<a id="add_battle_log"></a>

### `add_battle_log` — Add a battle log to a deck

write, additive · annotations `{"title":"Add a battle log to a deck","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

Attach a PTCG Live or in-person battle to a deck. A Live log is parsed server-side (result, opponent, turns, prizes, knockouts, opponent-deck guess) and attaches to the deck's CURRENT version — the list the game was played with — so per-version win/loss records accumulate. Parser-derived fields fill anything you omit. OMIT deck_id to rank the log against your decks first: the tool returns ranked candidate decks (real ids, names, scores) and writes nothing — call it again with deck_id set to the one you mean. dry_run defaults to TRUE: the first call only previews what would be logged without writing (with or without deck_id); re-call with dry_run: false to actually attach the log. The user's PTCG Live name from their DeckPal profile decides their side automatically when it appears in the log. If the parser cannot tell which player owns this deck it returns an error asking for player_name (the exact screen name in the log) or an explicit result — retry with one of those. Read logs back with battle_logs; to correct or remove an existing entry use edit_battle_log / delete_battle_log.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string |  |  | The deck, by UUID or by its exact name. OMIT to rank the log against your decks and pick — nothing is written. |
| `log` | string |  |  | The raw PTCG Live battle log text, pasted verbatim (max 50000 chars). Optional only for in_person/other. |
| `origin` | "ptcgl" \| "in_person" \| "other" |  |  | Where the game was played. Defaults to 'ptcgl' when log is present; required when log is absent. |
| `result` | "win" \| "loss" \| "tie" |  |  | Explicit result from the deck owner's perspective. Usually omit — the parser derives it; required for in_person/other, and required (or player_name) when a Live parser cannot identify the owner. |
| `player_name` | string |  |  | The deck owner's EXACT screen name as it appears in the log — pass when the tool reports it cannot identify the owner. |
| `opponent_deck` | string |  |  | Archetype label for the opponent's deck, e.g. 'Dragapult ex / Dusknoir'. The parser guesses when omitted. |
| `opponent_archetype` | string |  |  | Countable archetype key or label, e.g. 'dragapult-ex' or "N's Zoroark ex"; the API normalizes it. |
| `notes` | string |  |  | Free-text notes about the game — misplays, key turns, matchup reads. |
| `review` | string |  |  | Your own analysis of the game, in markdown. Keep the player's own words in notes. |
| `played_at` | string |  |  | ISO-8601 timestamp of when the game was played. Omit for now. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): parse and preview what would be logged, write nothing (works with or without deck_id). Re-call with dry_run: false to attach the log. |

<a id="battle_logs"></a>

### `battle_logs` — Read battle logs

read · annotations `{"title":"Read battle logs","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Read a deck's battle logs. Without log_id: a paged list, newest first (one compact row per game) with the win/loss record; filter to one deck version with version — that is the synthesis read path ("how did v2 do?"). With log_id: full detail for one log including all parsed fields plus the saved review. include_raw: true appends the raw PTCG Live log text when one exists — raw logs are LARGE (4–15k characters each), so list mode returns at most 3 a page; to judge a game, battle_digest is a small fraction of the size. Read-only. To record a game use add_battle_log; for version history use deck_history.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string | yes |  | The deck, by UUID or by NAME. |
| `log_id` | integer |  |  | One battle log id (from the list) → full detail instead of the list. |
| `version` | integer |  |  | List mode: only games played on this deck version. Omit for all versions. Ignored with log_id. |
| `include_raw` | boolean |  | `false` | Append the raw log text (the synthesis read path). Large — see the description for budget guidance. |
| `page` | integer |  | `1` | List page, starting at 1. |
| `page_size` | integer |  |  | Logs per page (default 50, cap 200; with include_raw, at most 3). |

<a id="deck_history"></a>

### `deck_history` — Deck version history and revert

write, destructive · annotations `{"title":"Deck version history and revert","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

Read a deck's version history, inspect one version, or revert. Versions exist because card (and format) changes to a version that already has battle logs create a NEW version, while changes to a logless version amend its snapshot in place — so each version is a list that actually saw play. With only deck_id: the version timeline (per-version W/L record, note, source, card count, current marker). With version: that snapshot in full plus the card diff vs the previous version. With revert_to: restore that version (cards, and its strategy guide unless include_strategy: false) — non-destructive: a revert ALWAYS lands as a new version, so the list it replaces stays in history even if it was never played, and history is never deleted. revert_to defaults to a dry run showing the exact card diff that would be applied; re-run with dry_run: false to execute. The result reports "created v<N>; v<N-1> keeps the list it replaced". Battle logs are read with battle_logs, not here.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string | yes |  | The deck, by UUID or by NAME — reverting needs the UUID or the exact name. |
| `version` | integer |  |  | Inspect this version: full card snapshot + diff vs the previous version. Not combinable with revert_to. |
| `revert_to` | integer |  |  | Restore this version's card list (must not be the current version). Dry-run by default. |
| `include_strategy` | boolean |  | `true` | Reverting only: also restore that version's strategy-guide snapshot (default true). |
| `note` | string |  |  | Reverting only: version note recorded on the change (default 'Reverted to v<k>'). |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | Reverting only. true (default): preview the exact diff, change nothing. false: execute the revert. |

### `edit_battle_log` — Correct a battle log entry

write, destructive, idempotent · annotations `{"title":"Correct a battle log entry","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Fix a battle log's metadata after the fact: result (e.g. the parser missed a non-standard ending and left NO RESULT), opponent name, opponent-deck label, countable archetype, notes, review, or played_at. The raw log text and the version it attaches to are immutable — this edits classification only, and per-version win/loss records recompute from it immediately. Passing null clears a field (not played_at). dry_run defaults to TRUE: the first call only previews the field-by-field changes (current → new) without writing; re-call with dry_run: false to apply. To remove an entry entirely use delete_battle_log; to add one use add_battle_log.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deck_id` | string | yes |  | The deck, by UUID or by its exact name. |
| `log_id` | integer | yes |  | Battle log id (the #N from battle_logs). |
| `result` | "win" \| "loss" \| "tie" or null |  |  | Corrected result from the deck owner's perspective; null clears it back to NO RESULT. |
| `opponent` | string or null |  |  | Opponent's screen name; null clears. |
| `opponent_deck` | string or null |  |  | Archetype label, e.g. 'Dragapult ex / Dusknoir'; null clears. |
| `opponent_archetype` | string or null |  |  | Normalized matchup key/label; the API normalizes it. null clears. |
| `notes` | string or null |  |  | Replacement notes; null clears. |
| `review` | string or null |  |  | Replacement analysis of the game, in markdown; null clears. The player's own words stay in notes. |
| `played_at` | string |  |  | Corrected ISO-8601 played-at timestamp. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): preview the field-by-field would-change plan (current → new), change nothing. Re-call with dry_run: false to apply the edit. |

### `delete_battle_log` — Delete a battle log entry

Permanently remove one battle log from a deck (e.g. a duplicate paste or a log attached to the wrong deck). Defaults to a dry run describing what would be deleted; re-run with dry_run: false to delete. To fix a wrong result/opponent instead, use edit_battle_log — deletion is not undoable.

### `battle_digest` — Read one game as a digest

Read ONE stored PTCG Live game as a compact digest: who went first, mulligans, turns, each side's first attack, the prize timeline turn by turn (with the Knock Out each prize paid for), every card the opponent showed, how it ended, whether it was close, and what the log cannot tell (their hand, the prized cards). <a id="edit_list"></a>

### `edit_list` — Create or edit a card list

write, destructive · annotations `{"title":"Create or edit a card list","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

Create a list (omit list_id) or edit one (pass list_id): rename, add cards, remove items, or restore a deleted list. add_cards takes the same card reference as log_cards — a TCGdex card_id, or name + set_id/number, plus an optional variant_kind ('reverse', 'holo', …) — so you do NOT need to look up variant ids first. add_missing does the whole job server-side: "everything missing for this goal in this set, optionally minus certain rarities or above a price" in one call. remove_item_ids are the item UUIDs shown by the lists tool. Renaming changes the name only, not what a list holds — to change contents use add_cards, add_missing or remove_item_ids. kind (static or dynamic) is set at create and cannot be changed by edit: a dynamic list tracks ownership live but does NOT re-filter by its name, so a list called "under $5" holds whatever was added, not every card under $5. Defaults to a dry run that prints the exact operations without executing — re-run with dry_run:false to apply. Lists never modify the collection itself.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | "create" \| "edit" |  |  | 'create' makes a NEW list and never touches an existing one, even if a list of the same name is already there. 'edit' changes the list named by list_id and never creates. Say which — if you leave it out it is inferred from list_id, and an inference is how an existing list gets written to by accident. |
| `list_id` | string |  |  | The list to EDIT, by UUID or by its exact name. Leave it out to create a new one. Ignored entirely when mode is 'create'. |
| `name` | string |  |  | List name — required when creating; renames when editing. |
| `kind` | "dynamic" \| "static" \| "pokedex_binder" |  | `"dynamic"` | List kind when creating (default 'dynamic'). Ignored when editing — kind cannot change. |
| `add_cards` | object[] |  |  | Cards to ADD (existing items are kept). Each entry: exactly one of card_id/name, variant_id, or dex_id. |
| `add_missing` | object |  |  | Add everything still missing from a set, filtered. Resolved server-side in one call. |
| `remove_item_ids` | string[] |  |  | Item UUIDs to remove (from the lists tool output), not card ids. |
| `restore` | boolean |  | `false` | true → restore this deleted list (see lists(deleted:true)). |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): only print what would happen. false: execute. |

<a id="delete_list"></a>

### `delete_list` — Delete a card list

write, destructive, idempotent · annotations `{"title":"Delete a card list","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Delete a list. By default this is REVERSIBLE: the list disappears from every view but is kept and can be restored with edit_list(list_id, restore:true), or found again with lists(deleted:true). The collection itself is never touched — lists only reference cards. Defaults to a dry run; re-run with dry_run:false to delete. purge:true is the exception: it destroys the list and its items for good, with no undo, and should only be used when the user has said they want it gone permanently. To remove individual items keep the list and use edit_list.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list_id` | string | yes |  | The list to delete, by UUID or by its exact name. |
| `purge` | boolean |  | `false` | true → destroy it permanently instead of moving it to the recycle bin. NO UNDO. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): only report what would be deleted. false: delete. |

<a id="log_cards"></a>

### `log_cards` — Log collection changes

write, destructive · annotations `{"title":"Log collection changes","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

Log card acquisitions/removals to the LOCAL DeckPal collection database — this edits only this app's collection tracker, nothing external (no store, no marketplace, no purchases). Batch of 1–250 items applied as ONE atomic transaction; each picks a card (card_id, or name + set_id/number), optionally a variant, and exactly one of delta (signed change, e.g. +1 pulled / -1 traded away) or quantity (absolute count). dry_run defaults to TRUE: the first call only previews current → new quantities; re-call with dry_run:false to actually write. Retrying after an error is SAFE — the batch carries an idempotency key, so a repeat returns the original result and writes nothing. Unresolvable or ambiguous items are reported individually and never guessed; the rest of the batch still applies. Do NOT use this to read history — use mutation_history or collection_log for that, and get_card for current quantities.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | object[] | yes |  | 1–250 changes to log, applied as ONE atomic batch. Each item picks a card (card_id, or name + set_id/number), optionally a variant, and exactly one of delta or quantity. |
| `note` | string |  |  | Optional free-text note stored on every event in this batch, e.g. 'pulls from 2 Prismatic packs'. |
| `idempotency_key` | string |  |  | Optional. Re-sending the same key returns the ORIGINAL result and writes nothing. Omit it and one is derived from the batch contents, which already makes a retry within ~15 minutes safe. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): preview current → new per item, write NOTHING. Re-call with false to apply. |

<a id="set_cart"></a>

### `set_cart` — Build TCGplayer cart links

read · annotations `{"title":"Build TCGplayer cart links","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

Build TCGplayer Mass Entry deep link(s) that pre-fill a shopping cart, from ONE of: a set (everything still needed for a goal), a saved list (list_id), or an explicit set of cards (items). Use list_id when you have already built and filtered a list — that way the cart contains exactly what the list contains, instead of being re-derived from the set. This tool only BUILDS links — it does not purchase anything, does not touch TCGplayer, and cannot add to a cart by itself: the user must open the link(s) in their own logged-in browser (a long list is split across several links; opening each adds to the same cart). Printing and condition cannot be preselected by link — they are chosen on TCGplayer's Mass Entry page. For what is missing and its cost use set_progress; for buying deck gaps use decks with include=[pricing].

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `set_id` | string |  |  | One set, by id ('me05') or by NAME. Carts what you still need from that set. |
| `list_id` | string |  |  | One list, by UUID or by NAME. Carts that list's own contents — nothing re-derived. |
| `items` | object[] |  |  | An explicit set of cards to cart, when you have not saved them as a list. Each needs variant_id or card_id. |
| `goal` | "complete" \| "master" \| "grandmaster" |  |  | set_id only. What 'needed' means: complete = one of any variant per card (default), master = every standard-tier variant, grandmaster = every variant. |
| `finishes` | "normal" \| "reverse" \| "holo" \| "lenticular" \| "metal"[] |  |  | set_id only. Restrict to these finishes (master/grandmaster; ignored for complete). |
| `rarity` | string[] |  |  | set_id only. ONLY these rarities, e.g. ['Illustration rare']. Case-insensitive, exact names. |
| `rarity_exclude` | string[] |  |  | set_id only. Leave these rarities OUT, e.g. ['Special illustration rare']. Note that variant tier ('standard'/'special') is NOT rarity — an Illustration Rare and a Special Illustration Rare are both tier 'standard', so use this rather than a tier filter. |
| `missing_only` | boolean |  | `false` | list_id only. true → cart only the list rows you do not already own. |

<a id="mutation_history"></a>

### `mutation_history` — What changed, and which operation changed it

read · annotations `{"title":"What changed, and which operation changed it","readOnlyHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

The audit trail of every CHANGE made through DeckPal — collection quantities, lists, decks, strategy guides — grouped by the operation that made them, newest first. Each operation carries who wrote it (web UI, deckpal-mcp, an import), an optional note, and one line per thing it touched (with the quantity before → after where there is one). Battle-log writes and deck_history reverts made over MCP are not recorded here. Filter by time, source, tool, note text, or a specific card/list/deck. Pass batch_id to see one operation's changes, paged. This is how you answer "what did that call actually do?" and it is the input to revert. For collection quantities only, collection_log is a flatter view of the same events.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_id` | string |  |  | Show ONE operation and every change in it. From a previous mutation_history call or a log_cards result. |
| `since` | string |  |  | Only operations at/after this ISO 8601 timestamp, e.g. '2026-08-19T02:00:00Z'. |
| `until` | string |  |  | Only operations at/before this ISO 8601 timestamp. |
| `source` | string |  |  | Only operations written by this source, e.g. 'web', 'deckpal-mcp'. |
| `tool` | string |  |  | Only this operation type, e.g. 'collection.batch', 'list.delete', 'revert'. |
| `note` | string |  |  | Only operations whose note contains this text (case-insensitive substring). |
| `entity_type` | "collection_item" \| "card_list" \| "list_item" \| "deck" \| "deck_card" \| "deck_strategy" \| "battle_log" |  |  | Only operations that touched this kind of thing. |
| `entity_id` | string |  |  | Only operations that touched this exact thing (a numeric card_variant id, or a list/deck UUID). |
| `limit` | integer |  |  | Per page (1–200): operations (default 25), or with batch_id that operation's changes (default 50). |
| `page` | integer |  | `1` | Page number, 1-based. |

<a id="revert"></a>

### `revert` — Undo a change

write, destructive · annotations `{"title":"Undo a change","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

Undo something DeckPal did: a whole operation (batch_id), one change (event_id), everything since a moment (since), or every change to one card/list/deck (entity_type + entity_id). Defaults to a DRY RUN that prints the exact before → after for each item and changes nothing — re-call with dry_run:false to apply. Quantities are undone by applying the opposite change, so unrelated later edits survive; pass strategy:"restore" to force the old value back instead. Where an exact undo is impossible (the original change hit the zero floor, or a later call asserted an absolute quantity for that card) the item is reported as a CONFLICT and skipped rather than half-applied. The revert is itself logged, so it can be reverted. Use mutation_history first to find what to undo.

| argument | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_id` | string |  |  | Undo this whole operation (from mutation_history or a log_cards result). |
| `event_id` | integer |  |  | Undo one single change. |
| `since` | string |  |  | Undo every change at/after this ISO 8601 timestamp, e.g. '2026-08-19T02:00:00Z'. |
| `until` | string |  |  | With since: stop at this timestamp. |
| `filter_source` | string |  |  | With since: only undo changes written by this source, e.g. 'web' or 'deckpal-mcp' (mutation_history calls the same filter `source`). Omit to undo EVERYTHING in the window regardless of who wrote it. |
| `entity_type` | "collection_item" \| "card_list" \| "list_item" \| "deck" \| "deck_strategy" |  |  | With entity_id: undo changes to one thing. |
| `entity_id` | string |  |  | The card_variant id (numeric) or list/deck UUID to roll back. |
| `at` | string |  |  | With entity_type + entity_id: roll that one thing back to how it was at this time. |
| `strategy` | "inverse" \| "restore" |  | `"inverse"` | inverse (default): apply the opposite change, leaving unrelated later edits alone. restore: force the value back to what it was, discarding anything that happened since. |
| `force` | boolean |  | `false` | Apply items that have conflicts, or re-undo something already undone. Read the dry run first. |
| `note` | string |  |  | Note stored on the revert operation itself. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `true` | true (default): show the exact diff, change nothing. false: apply. |
